subject: Throughput smoothing plan and autoscale soft-override
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng@horizon-ai.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput smoothing plan and autoscale soft-override

Team —

Horizon flagged a risk for their Q3 pilot: they expect a 3x spike in model concurrency for two 48-hour windows (mid-Aug and early Sep) tied to scheduled load tests with an external partner. They asked for a short-term capacity guarantee and lower tail latency during those windows.

We discussed two options on the product side: (A) reserve a temporary dedicated slice for the pilot weeks, or (B) allow a controlled autoscale "soft-override" that bumps their priority curve for the window without changing long-term reservations. Procurement is pushing back on reservations for a small pilot; they prefer option B if ops can guarantee no noisy-neighbor regressions.

Ask: Marcus/Karthik — can infra ops (gpu-pool) provide a proposed smoothing policy that:
- increases effective throughput for Horizon by ~2.5x at 95th percentile for those windows,
- limits cross-customer preemption risk,
- includes a rollback runbook if latency degrades beyond threshold?

I'm attaching a one-pager with customer timelines and a first-draft runbook. Please reply with what we can commit to by EOD Thu so I can lock expectations with Horizon.

Thanks,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Product — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
[attachment: throughput-smoothing-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput smoothing plan and autoscale soft-override

Kimberly —

Thanks for the context and the attach. Short answer: yes, we can do a controlled soft-override, but there are trade-offs and a few constraints we need to bake in. High-level notes from infra:  

1) Mechanism: implement a temporary priority-curve shift + shorter autoscale cooldown during the window. This behaves like a surge policy, not a reservation — after the window we revert.

2) Limits: to protect other customers we must cap the maximum absolute GPU fraction per tenant (e.g., 40% of a single pool) and ensure preemption happens only on best-effort workloads, not on SLA-backed Dedicated customers.

3) Observability and rollback: we'll add a synthetic latency check and token-cost burn guard. If p95 increases > 50ms or token cost exceeds threshold X for 5 continuous minutes, the system auto-reverts the soft-override.

4) Runbook: I drafted steps (see attached runbook md) for toggling the policy, monitoring signals, stakeholder pings, and escalation path to SRE. Need input from Karthik on exact metric IDs and from Monica on comms cadence.

I can get a proof-of-concept config and runbook ready by Thu EOD. If Horizon requires stricter guarantees, we'll need a short-term reserved slice (procurement discussion).

-Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
[attachment: autoscale-soft-override-runbook.md (Markdown)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, eng@horizon-ai.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput smoothing plan and autoscale soft-override

Thanks Marcus — this sounds reasonable. A couple of product/contracting constraints from my side:  

- Horizon's commercial asks are that the smoothing is "no-risk" for their pilot. They will accept soft-override language if we cover two things in writing: 1) explicit rollback triggers (you listed), and 2) a credit formula if we fail to revert within 30 minutes after a trigger.

- We should avoid changing pool-level caps for SLA-backed Dedicated customers. Instead, apply a short-term tenant-level cap as Marcus suggested.

Operational asks: can we create a temporary policy id that ties to the Horizon customer id and expiry timestamp so it's auditable and automatically expires? Also request a short resourcing note: who on SRE will be on-call for the window?

I'll hold commercial on a green light until we have the runbook, synthetic checks, and the credit formula drafted.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Throughput smoothing plan and autoscale soft-override

Looping in a quick plan from customer success: Horizon's pilot kickoff is Aug 12; first load window is Aug 18-19, second is Sep 6-7. They want minimum notice of 72 hours for any infra changes.

Proposed customer comms:
- Tue Aug 13: "We will enable temporary throughput smoothing from Aug 18 00:00 UTC to Aug 20 00:00 UTC; monitor latency and revert if thresholds hit."
- Fri Sep 5: same note for Sep window.

SRE on-call: I'll book Rohan Mehta (ops) as primary and Marcus as secondary for the windows. We'll also create a public Doc with the toggle time and expected metrics.

Also adding suggested credit language for sales: "If soft-override remains active longer than 30 minutes after a defined trigger, customer receives a prorated credit equal to 1 day's hosting fee for the affected pilot window." Please review.

-Monica

--
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: eng@horizon-ai.com, rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput smoothing plan and autoscale soft-override

All —

We validated the approach in staging this morning. Quick summary of what went into the final runbook and config (attached):
- Policy id: soft-override-horizon-DL4491-202508 (auto-expires 2025-08-21T00:00:00Z for the Aug window)
- Max tenant GPU fraction: 38% per pool
- Autoscale cooldown reduced to 20s during window
- Synthetic check: p95-token-latency-horizon (5m sliding window) + token-cost-burn metric
- Auto-revert if p95 increases > 50ms for 5 continuous minutes or cost burn exceeds threshold

I've uploaded the final runbook to the shared doc and wired the Jira ticket JIRA-OPS-7821 to notify SRE when the toggle is flipped. Rohan confirmed on-call acceptance and will be primary for the Aug window.

Next steps for Sales/Product: please confirm the customer comms timeline and credit formula. Once confirmed, I'll schedule the change for the August window and create the audit entry.

Thanks — Marcus

--
